Front: Where can you find the rules governing a lawyer's conduct?
Back: In legislation (Legal Professional Act) & subsidiary legislation (Legal Professional Conduct Rules)

Front: Must lawyers follow the legal ethics?
Back: yes it is part of the profession!

Front: What are the 4 categories of lawyer obligations?
Back:
- obligations to the client (most practical)
- obligations to the Court (most crucial)
- obligations to other Counsel
- obligations to society (provide access to justice)

- Competence

- Ensure that you
have the ability in that area of the Law

- If not, refer
client to somebody else who has greater knowledge

- Loyalty

- Cannot act against
your Client’s interest

- Ensure that there
is no Conflict of Interest

- Current and Past
Client having conflict of interest

- This is an issue
for big firms, where one lawyer might be handling a case against
another lawyer in same firm

- Client
Confidentiality

- Clients must be
able to hire a lawyer and strategise together

- Client must be able
to have candour and be forthcoming

- Only several
occasions when you can talk about client’s case

- Abstract Manner
(no names mentioned)

- Only if client indicates that he would be
committing another imminent crime. In this case, Lawyer is obliged to
discharge from case or inform the court.

- Lawyers should not
misrepresent the Law to the Court

- Despite being an
adversarial process, lawyers do not only have a duty to the client.

- As an officer of the court, lawyers cannot
misrepresent facts or law or hide which are damaging to his client.

- Duty of Candour →
To be forthcoming to the court, so as to allow for the court to have full
knowledge to make a fair judgment

- Duty of Discovery (giving opposing lawyer
complete evidence)

- No faking of
evidence.

- No coaxing of
clients to make false statements.

- About
a balancing act → First and paramount duty is always to the court → if
client insists on misrepresenting facts, lawyer has to withdraw from case

- Honouring
Undertakings (especially important in Admiralty Law)

- Do not talk to other Counsel’s clients

- Good Faith – Giving other
people 2-day notice to prepare for certain actions

- Access to justice irrespective of financial means of the person that seeks justice

- Balance between law
as a business (making money), and their public duty as officers of the
court to offer services on a reasonable basis (in terms of time available
to them) to people who need it
- Do not give somebody the impression that you are
acting for them when you are actually not

Inspire lawyers to reach ethical goals
e.g. 2015 Rule: Any legal
practitioner or law practice may contribute to good causes, whether by way of
donation, sponsorship, subscription or the provision of free services; and any
contribution made by the legal practitioner or law practice may be publicly acknowledged

Impose penalties.

practitioner or law practice must not enter into any negotiations with a client

● Made in writing to the Council of Law
Society

● Includes a statement by the complainant —
whether to his knowledge, any other complaint has been made to the Society
about the same legal practitioner by him or other persons that arises from the
same facts as the lodged complaint

● Could also be initiated when the AG/Supreme
Court refers information on the conduct of one of its members to the Council

● Council may initiate proceedings on its own
volition

● Appointed
by the Chief Justice

● Consists of local and regulated foreign
lawyers, and lay persons

● Term of 2 years and can be renewed

● Consists of

○ A Chairperson who is part of the Inquiry
Panel as a Chair/Deputy Chairperson, or a lawyer 12 years’ experience who is
part of the Inquiry Panel

○ Either:

■ (Accused local lawyer) Legal/Judicial
services officer with at least 10 years’ experience

■ (Accused foreign lawyer) Foreign lawyer
with at least 10 years’ experience who is part of the Inquiry Panel

● Begins review of legal practitioner’s
profile and may interview him

● Reports back to the Council of the Law Society

● Acts
as a gatekeeper to prevent frivolous allegations from clogging the disciplinary
process

● Formed by the Chairperson of the Inquiry
Panel

● Consists of

○ Chairperson of the Inquiry Panel (being a
member of the Inquiry Panel who is an advocate and solicitor of not less than
12 years’ standing)

○ Member of the Inquiry Panel (Local/Foreign lawyer depending
on the status of the defendant legal practitioner)

○ Member of the Inquiry Panel (Lay person)

○ Person with at least 10 years experience as
a Judicial Service Officer/Legal Service Officer (or both)

● Commences inquiry within 2 weeks of
appointment

● Have to address the question of the
necessity of formal investigation by a Disciplinary Tribunal and recommend to
Council if it should take place.

● If there is no need for a formal
investigation by DT, they can advise under Section 88 for legal practitioner to
pay penalty, be reprimanded, ordered to comply with remedial measures, or
dismiss the complaint

● Inquiry Committee’s report will be
considered by LawSoc, then LawSoc will produce its own findings within a month

● If there is a need for formal
investigation, the Society will apply to CJ to appoint DT to hear and
investigate matter within 4 weeks

● Reports back to Council of the Law Society

○ Whether there is a need for Disciplinary
Tribunal

○ If not, what penalties or whether case is
dismissed

● Appointed by the Chief Justice

○ Consists of:

■ President (Senior Counsel, or Senior
Judge/ex-Supreme Court Judge/JC)

■ Local/foreign lawyer with at least 12
years’ experience

● Makes a determination of findings

○ 3 possible conclusions:

■ No cause of sufficient gravity warranting
disciplinary action,

■ While no cause exists, the advocate and
solicitor should nevertheless be reprimanded and ordered to pay a penalty commensurate
with the character of his misconduct; and

■ A cause of sufficient gravity for
disciplinary action exists.

○ Council
may agree and strike lawyer off roll (suspension from practice)

● LawSoc Council will refer the matter to the
C3J

● Show Cause hearing: onus is on the lawyer
to defend himself before the Court of 3 Judges to prove he is innocent. (case
law will be discussed when litigating the case)

○ Lawyer can represent himself or get an
advocate

■ The Court of 3 Judges does not sit as an
appeal court against the decision of the tribunal → merely allows the lawyer
the opportunity to give reasons as to why he should not be disciplined

○ Standard of Proof is beyond reasonable
doubt, not on balance of probabilities

○ If there is a defect with the decision of
the tribunal, the Court of 3 Judges may set aside the tribunal’s decision.

● Essentially, the C3J have the final say
over the pronouncement of guilt over a transgression and the level and type of
punishment meted out

○ Fine, Suspension, Disqualification

○ Usually to do with the “ability to
practice” rather than a punishment or fine

● Full power to determine any question
regarding the case

● Can direct DT to reinvestigate or rehear
proceedings

Once reheard proceedings are satisfactory, the
decision is submitted as final and the legal practitioner cannot appeal

Group 1 Lawyers

Group 2 Lawyers

Group 3 Lawyers

More than 8 months of practicing certificate: 8 CPD Points

b.

(The morally right action is the one that
produced the greatest balance of happiness over unhappiness for the
greatest number of people.)

- Define
the facts

- List the
stakeholders (who will be affected)

- Define
the ethical issue (e.g. conflicting rights)

- Identify
major rules/principles/values (e.g. integrity)
- Identify
alternative courses of action

- Compare values and alternatives. Is
